title: Improve Auto LOD Generation on Mesh Import
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in Godot 4.5.1+ ### System information Linux Mint - Godo 4.5.1 - Vulkan (Forward+) ### Issue description Related to issue #64751, please see existing discussion related to [meshoptimizer](https://github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer). Relevant To: Any 3D project using Generate LODs for mesh on import. Premise: It's important to keep our Draw Calls as low as possible. For a specific numerical target, consoles often try to optimize between 2000-3000 draw calls ([source](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/programming/gpu-performance-for-game-artists)). Problem: Generate LODs returns an unbounded number of LODs. Each LOD results in a unique draw call, which compounds quickly. Bonus Complication: Each LOD is also going to experience shadow cascades, which multiplies into our LOD count. With default settings, there are 4 shadow cascades. So we can imagine a common-worst case scenario, a single tree copied around our play level may experience: 1 (one unique mesh) * 5 (shadow cascades) * 10 (LODs) = 50 Draw Calls. Desired Solution: It would be nice to cap our auto-LOD counts on a project settings level. A dream would be auto-generation of billboards as well, but I do not know how difficult that would be to achieve. It would wonderful if we could, on a project settings level, request that our final LOD level is a billboard. ### Steps to reproduce Here is a short test to illustrate our unbounded and poorly tuned LODs, Here's a reasonably dense mesh in Blender. `meshoptimzer` will supposedly generate more LODs for denser objects, Now, an empty level with a control node to help us see the Monitor readout, Let's add 5 objects close to the camera. We should expect Draw Calls to increase by one, which it does, Now let's move one of the objects a small distance back to trigger an LOD transition. We have have an extra Draw Call, Let's do that again, note the draw calls again incrementing, Now all 5 objects are spaced out, with positions: -2, -7, -92, -224, -1037. This final example shows how horribly tuned LOD transitions are by default. LOD2 is entirely invisible, but it's still followed by LOD3 and LOD4 here. I do not know if more LODs were generated by meshoptimizer for this sample mesh, I stopped my test here. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [batch-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26054915/batch-test.zip)
